record.original_question: Let K be the four sides of a square of side length ℓ. Determine a curve or barrier C of minimal total length, contained inside the square, with the property that every straight line that meets K also meets C.

evidence.quote: trouver une courbe C de longueur minimale, contenue dans le carré, telle que toute droite coupant K coupe aussi C.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be the closed unit square in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with side length $\ell>0$, and let $K=\partial S$ denote its boundary (the union of its four sides). A subset $C\subseteq S$ is called an opaque barrier for $S$ if every straight line in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that intersects $K$ also intersects $C$. For a sufficiently regular set $C$ (for example, a finite union of rectifiable curves), let $\mathcal{L}(C)$ denote its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (total length).

Determine
$$ m(\ell) \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\,\mathcal{L}(C)\;:\; C\subseteq S\text{ is an opaque barrier for }S\,\bigr\}, $$
and exhibit a curve (or finite system of curves) $C^\star\subseteq S$ that attains this infimum, or prove that no minimizer exists. In particular, decide whether the configuration consisting of the Steiner minimal tree of three vertices of the square together with the segment joining the fourth vertex to the center—of total length $\sqrt{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,\ell$ when $\ell=1$—is optimal.
artifact.status_search_result: The opaque square problem remains open. The best known upper bound for a (possibly disconnected) opaque barrier of the unit square is approximately 2.6389, achieved by the Steiner tree of three vertices together with a segment joining the fourth vertex to the center; the best general lower bound is 2 (Jones, ca. 1970s). It is unknown whether the upper-bound construction is optimal.

status_evidence.title: Opaque set - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A shorter, disconnected opaque forest is known, with length approximately 2.639... It is unproven whether this is the shortest possible opaque set for the square.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality of the best known opaque barrier for the unit square is unproven.

status_evidence.title: The opaque square (Dumitrescu-Jiang)
status_evidence.snippet: Best known lower bound for the length of an opaque barrier of the unit square is 2.
status_evidence.claim: Gap between known upper and lower bounds remains; problem is open.
